I'm a mod of a new subverse, and i'm trying to make my sub engaging for people to get involved and want to join it. Yes its taxing and after a recent discussion with another mod about this where we both agreed that getting publicity is and issue and that mods and subverse's could do with helping each other in a community based fashion. Here are some of the suggestions:

  • Advertising subs in the sidebar. BUT ensuring a two way system so its not entirely one sided to ensure maximum efficiency and potential of using this method. Afterall, no one likes advertising. (probably the nicest and less protruding system)

  • Making use of the sticky. One day a week for a period of time having a sticky with a load of subs people could add. It would support the small communities of voat and allow them to gain more traffic without being too intrusive on the feed.

  • Another similar method is having a day in the week for a period of time where users are allowed to advertise their subs where it gets deleted after that period of time within the day. So it wouldn't be so intruding.

  • Cross-sub competitions. Rather than blatantly advertising the sub, advertise an event going in the sub. For example /v/aquariumdiy this sub could advertise an aquarium design competition to a design or art based sub for people to enter and that would increase traffic for that small community. Another example is my sub /v/Bettafish could hold photography competitions that are advertised in a photography sub which actually creates opportunities for the community of Voat and allows people to contribute and get involved.

Those are the ones for now. Obviously, the whole newsubverses thing is great, except you can only post once and not everyone who may want to subscribe to your subverse will see it, especially with the influx of new users joining daily. My posts to newsubverses are likely to have gotten buried now and might not be found so easily.

Another thing thats been mentioned is that obviously, no one likes advertising and it could for a fact drive people away especially if these subs don't align to their interests. Its hard to get the balance.

We need each other to make this place great. But how do we get the attention the small subverses need to make lift off, without upsetting everyone? There's a subverse for everyone, you have the general ones, but everybody has hobbies. That one specific subverse you always go to related to that specific interest or hobby, that's likely a smaller community than the general ones of voat.

ANY suggestions or thoughts about this dilemma will be appreciated
What would you suggest as good ideas to get small subverse's the traffic they need to get going, without compromising the needs of the subscribers, but also allows subverse's to help each other?

Subverse partnerships. Allow subs with similar interest, but different goals, to link together somehow.

Things that could be done between partnered subs:

  1. Featured posts. Could be handled different ways.

-- The top post from sub A is automatically featured in sub B

-- Mods from sub A recommend (to the mods of sub B) a post they think represents their sub positively. Sub B mods decide to feature it or not.

-- Have a 'Partnered Subs' list, similar to how mods currently link to similar subs, but this will be higher up on the sidebar, larger and fancier to draw attention. A partnered sub also carries the recommendation of the mods from a sub you enjoy.

  1. Sub crossovers. Have days where representatives from sub A run a question day in sub B and vice versa.

  2. Partnered subs that are small can somehow get a small boost to their post ranking to give them more visibility on /v/all.

  3. Partnered subs could have their subs featured as a 'collection' where the mods can come up with a small graphic to show in the feature spot that when clicked goes straight to a multiverse of those partnered subs.

  4. Multiverses for partnered subs. Say a bunch of makeup/beauty subs decide to partner up. Their central point (that the aforementioned feature wpuld point to) might be /mv/beautification (/mv/ for multiverse?) which is a central hub for all those subs with an interface to navigate to specifics.

  5. For subs that might not attract css geniuses, getting a few css gods together that are willing to put their hands up to help others get their style right will help small subs feel like home.

I know some of these things can be done manually, but providing a platform to make it easier for mods and to make the impact of them more significant is a good thing, right? After all that is what's killing Reddit.
